To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) exploit dependency graphs can represent all possible attack paths; (2) exploit dependency graphs have polynomial complexity; (3) initial conditions (network hardening measures) can be represented as sets of exploits; (4) exploit dependency graphs enable efficient computation of minimum-cost hardening measures that guarantee safety of given resources; and (5) exploit dependency graphs allow for the resolution of exploit redundancies and irrelevancies that cannot be resolved by previous approaches.

the problem of computing a minimal-cost initial network condition that guarantees the safety of a given set of critical resources, given a set of exploits with associated costs, can be reduced to computing a minimal-cost assignment of a finite number of Boolean variables.
we can compute efficient minimum-cost initial conditions that ensure the safety of given network resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
efficient, scalable methods for computing network hardening measures that guarantee the safety (or security) of given critical resources, given the costs of hardening measures.
efficient computation of minimum-cost initial conditions that guarantee the safety (or, more precisely, the non-attainability) of critical resources.

the following problem: Given a network of resources and their vulnerabilities, and given the costs associated with hardening measures, find the cheapest set of hardening measures to ensure that no attacker can compromise the network's critical resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is more efficient, more precise, and more complete than previous approaches.
our approach is the most efficient and complete way to date to find minimum-cost network hardenings.
our approach is efficient in terms of time and space, it is complete (it finds all solutions), and it is sound and correct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a polynomial-time, minimum-cost, network-hardening algorithm that is more efficient and more effective than previous approaches.

, given a network, a set of critical resources, and costs associated with network hardening measures, our method efficiently computes a set of initial network conditions that guarantees the safety of the given critical resources and minimizes overall costs.
we have proposed an efficient, practical approach to network hardening that can be used for large networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

network hardening can be done efficiently and effectively by considering the full space of possible exploit combinations, not just the most likely combinations, which are typically considered in previous work.
, in order to minimize the costs associated with network hardening, one must consider not just exploit combinations, but initial network conditions as well.
, by using a suitable exploit-dependency representation, one can compute minimum-cost hardening assignments efficiently.
